etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English violent, from Old French violent, from Latin violentus, from vīs (“strength”). Displaced native Old English stræc. For the verb, compare French violenter.

quote.citation: 1749, Henry Fielding, The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling, volume (please specify |volume=I to VI), London: A[ndrew] Millar, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: We have already observed, that he was a very good-natured fellow, and he hath himself declared the violent attachment he had to the person and character of Jones  […]

definitions.definition: Produced or effected by force; not spontaneous; unnatural.
